correctness.rationale: Explicit contraction maps competing perfect matchings bijectively to directed cycles. Acyclicity reduces optimal deletions to maximizing forward available arcs. The forbidden arcs are the cycle cover of the derangement: each directed cycle forces at least one missing forward arc, with equality by reversed cyclic orders, yielding exactly n(n-3)/2+c(pi). Standard cycle decomposition and labeled exponential formula give the polynomial; the integer recurrence and endpoint counts are independently derived. Every symbolic boundary n>=3 and deletion domain E(G)\M checked. The accompanying verifier independently exhausts all topological orders through n=6 and direct matching-obstruction hitting sets at n=3,4. No infinite result rests on finite tests.

value.rationale: The exact minimum deletion problem for a dense bipartite family with exponentially/factorially many matchings has a meaningful cycle-type phase structure: all matchings have the same ordinary forcing number n-2 in earlier work, yet their anti-forcing numbers realize a full floor(n/2)-wide interval and have associated-Stirling multiplicities. Acyclic order rigidity also explicitly classifies every optimal deletion construction and supports computations of extremal distributions.
